sanskrit_verse:
आत्मनोऽर्थे क्रियारम्भो मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम् ।
स्वाध्यायाग्निसुतत्यागो बान्धवत्याग एव च ॥३-२३९॥
transliteration: ātmano'rthe kriyārambho madyapastrīniṣevaṇam | svādhyāyāgnisutatyāgo bāndhavatyāga eva ca || 3.239 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Engagement in action for the sake of the Self; indulgence in wine and women; abandonment of study, fire ritual, and progeny; and renunciation of family—these constitute the marks of one who has withdrawn from worldly dharmic obligations.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from alignment with conscious dharma, not social role
Causation is traced through withdrawal from sustaining duties
Capacity-based responsibility diminishes with disengagement from societal dharma
Restoration logic requires reintegration into sustaining relationships and practices
Consciousness alignment necessitates return to svadharma as revealed by the Self
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual abandons svādhyāya THEN legal recognition of diminished societal duty capacity
IF an individual engages in habitual madyapastrīniṣevaṇam THEN initiate consciousness-realignment protocol
IF an individual withdraws from agnisautram OR progeny THEN invoke community-integrity restoration process
IF bāndhavatyāga is observed THEN activate kinship-reconnection framework
IF kriyārambha is absent without declared spiritual intent THEN trigger dharma-status review
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes a threshold for recognizing voluntary withdrawal from societal dharmic roles. Legal standing must reflect whether such withdrawal is rooted in conscious renunciation or mere avoidance. Authority is reassigned based on demonstrated capacity to uphold or release dharma.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that cessation of dharma-sustaining acts leads to natural diminishment of societal integration. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential detachment from svadharma. Responsibility is proportional to sustained engagement. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that withdrawal results in organic loss of influence, not imposed penalty.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svadharma re-engagement inquiry to assess conscious intent
Deploy śruti-based guidance to reconnect individual with sustaining practices
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this declaration affirms Dharma as non-punitive, consciousness as the ultimate adjudicator, and restoration as the sole purpose of legal alignment. All beings are restored to their svadharma when guided by the Self.
